sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: This repository is a single CLAUDE.md file of coding guidelines that makes Claude Code behave more carefully. It's based on Andrej Karpathy's observations about common mistakes language models make when writing code, and it works as a Claude Code plugin or a file you drop into your project.
sixtySeconds.problem: AI coding agents often assume things without asking, overcomplicate code, and change code they weren't asked to touch. Four short principles in this file push the agent to state assumptions, keep things simple, make only the requested changes, and work toward checkable goals.
whoFor: Claude Code users who want fewer unwanted changes
Developers tired of overengineered AI-written code
Teams standardising how coding agents behave
Cursor users, through the included project rule
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a tiny, readable set of rules you can merge with your own project instructions. The README notes it favours caution over speed, so use judgement on trivial tasks.
requirements: Claude Code (plugin or CLAUDE.md), or Cursor

overview: The file contains four principles. Think Before Coding asks the agent to state assumptions, present interpretations and ask when unsure. Simplicity First asks for the minimum code that solves the problem with nothing speculative. Surgical Changes limits edits to what the request needs. Goal-Driven Execution turns tasks into verifiable goals, such as writing a failing test first and then making it pass.

You can install it as a Claude Code plugin from its marketplace, which makes it available across all your projects, or download the CLAUDE.md into a single project or append it to an existing one. The repository also includes a Cursor project rule so the same guidelines apply in Cursor.

The README lists signs it's working: fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites caused by overcomplication, clarifying questions before implementation, and clean, minimal pull requests. It's designed to be combined with your own project-specific rules. The README states an MIT license.

steps.body: For example a section listing your language settings, testing rules and error-handling patterns.
steps.code:
## Project-Specific Guidelines

- Use TypeScript strict mode
- All API endpoints must have tests
- Follow the existing error handling patterns in `src/utils/errors.ts`

steps.title: Give the agent goals it can verify
steps.body: Instead of "Fix the bug", ask it to write a test that reproduces the bug, then make it pass.

tutorial.expected: Claude Code asks clarifying questions before implementing, keeps changes minimal, and produces smaller, cleaner diffs.
